name: Times club monthly special crossword No 20,196

solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Star of Brexit all washed up

indicators.note: something washed up is wrecked and scattered, so the letters before it are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A political pundit declares that a leading light of Brexit is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: BREXIT ALL rearranges to BELLATRIX, the bright star in Orion's shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bellatrix is the name of one of the brightest stars in the constellation Orion.

clue.text: Mature crowd after reverse accepting defeat

indicators.note: going into reverse means the word for a crowd is written back to front
to accept is to take something in, so the reversed crowd wraps around the defeat

blocks.note: a mob is an unruly crowd
a loss is a defeat in a contest

explanation.surface: A crowd backs away while conceding a defeat, like a team reversing out of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mature' is a verb here, as in coming into flower, not the adjective it looks like beside 'crowd'.
explanation.definitionFit: To blossom is to develop fully and come into flower, a verb sense of maturing or ripening.

clue.text: Solution something impossible for Washington to announce?

indicators.note: announcing is saying out loud, so we want a word that sounds like the thing described

blocks.note: George Washington supposedly said he could not tell a falsehood

explanation.surface: A wry question about what George Washington could never bring himself to say.
explanation.walkthrough: The legend has young George Washington confess to cutting the cherry tree with 'I cannot tell a lie'; LIE sounds like LYE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lye is a strongly alkaline liquid made by leaching wood ash, used in soap making, so a chemical solution.

clue.text: Wise men cautious when pursuing answer

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so these words come after the letter for answer

blocks.note: A is the usual abbreviation for answer
chary means wary or cautious
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Sages being careful before giving any reply.
explanation.definitionFit: An acharya is a Hindu spiritual teacher or learned guru, so acharyas are revered sages.

clue.text: Laugh cousin’s thus got from Corin?

blocks.note: the letter of this name that must change
the apostrophe s read as is
the two letters this word has where the shepherd's name has its third letter

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how one cousin's laugh was picked up from Corin, the shepherd in As You Like It.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is an instruction: you get COUSIN from CORIN if R IS US, i.e. replace the R with US. Read as a phrase, R IS US gives RISUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Risus is the Latin word for a laugh or grin, kept in English dictionaries as a rare learned term.

clue.text: Tree by lane on the inside, however large, needs cutting with axes

indicators.note: the inside of a word is its middle, so only the central letters of lane are kept
cutting into something means going inside it, so an axis letter splits the size letters

blocks.note: X is the multiplication sign, as in three by four
the two middle letters of the word
tho is an informal short spelling of though, meaning however
XL is the clothing size extra large
Y names one of the axes of a graph, the y-axis

explanation.surface: A woodsman's instruction: a large tree by the lane must be felled with axes.
explanation.walkthrough: X + AN + THO, then XL with Y cutting into it gives X(Y)L. Axes in the surface are choppers; in the wordplay they are graph axes.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanthoxyl is the prickly ash, a genus of aromatic shrubs and small trees whose bark is used medicinally.

clue.text: Eager, finding way back in no matter what

indicators.note: going back means the abbreviation for a way is written in the other direction
in tells us the reversed way sits inside the phrase that follows

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
any, as in any one at all, no matter which

explanation.surface: Someone keen to get home by whatever route is going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No matter what' looks like an emphatic phrase but supplies a three-letter word meaning whichever.
explanation.definitionFit: Antsy means restless and impatient, keen for something to happen, a colloquial near-synonym of eager.

clue.text: No longer admit part in freezing allowances, upset

indicators.note: a part in a phrase is a run of its letters, so the answer is lodged inside the following words
in a down clue upset turns the hidden letters upside down, so they read from the bottom

blocks.note: the letters running across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A grumble about being refused a share of benefits during a freeze on allowances.
explanation.walkthrough: freEZING Allowances holds EZINGA, which read upwards gives AGNIZE. 'No longer' marks the word as obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnize is an obsolete verb meaning to acknowledge or recognise, so it is an old word for admit.

clue.text: Infant, one with friends describing some birds’ feet

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
I is the Roman numeral for one
two words for a friend, pal and mate, side by side

explanation.surface: A child and a companion watch some birds and describe their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural friends supplies two friends, PAL and MATE, giving TOT + I + PAL + MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: Totipalmate is the term for feet with all four toes joined by webbing, as in pelicans and cormorants.

clue.text: To go on horse, fancy fellow produces icebox

blocks.note: to yak is to chatter on at length
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H
dan is an old honorific title, like Master or Sir, for a man of standing

explanation.surface: A dandy who rides off on horseback comes up with a cool box.
explanation.definitionFit: A yakhdan is a Persian chest or box for carrying ice and keeping food cold, especially on a pack animal.

clue.text: Old trees, not English, African ones

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for English is taken out of the trees

blocks.note: O is the standard abbreviation for old
beeches are common broadleaf trees
E abbreviates English; one of its two copies is dropped

explanation.surface: Ancient trees that are not native to England but come from Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: O + BEECHES with one E removed gives OBECHES. 'Ones' in the definition stands in for trees.
explanation.definitionFit: The obeche is a large West African tree whose pale, light timber is widely exported, so obeches are African trees.

clue.text: Sister, with a brief snatch, getting the point of rock

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the word for a snatch loses its final letter

blocks.note: a nun is a religious sister
taken as written
to take is to seize or snatch

explanation.surface: A nun grabs something and finally understands what all the fuss is about.
explanation.walkthrough: TAKE shortened is TAK, giving NUN + A + TAK. 'Getting the point' reads as understanding; the point is a peak.
explanation.definitionFit: A nunatak is a rocky peak standing up through an ice sheet or glacier, a pinnacle of stone.

clue.text: Scot who predicts cuts will return

indicators.note: returning is coming back, so the word for cuts is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to reap is to cut a crop

explanation.surface: A Scottish soothsayer forecasts that spending cuts are coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: A spaer is the Scots word for a fortune-teller or prophet, from spae, to foretell.

clue.text: Banner unfurled over holiday home after a nickel is found in it

indicators.note: an unfurled flag is spread out of its folds, so these letters are opened up into a new order
after places the shuffled flag letters behind the single letter a

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters as written, to be rearranged
a gite is a French holiday cottage

explanation.surface: A banner is unrolled above a holiday cottage once some nickel has been found there.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the anagram above GITE: A + NNABER + GITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Annabergite is a green mineral, a hydrated nickel arsenate, so nickel is one of its main constituents.

clue.text: Crustacean from Australia turned over in fragment in turf

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the nickname for Australia is read backwards
in places each piece inside the next, nesting them like boxes

blocks.note: a sod is a clump of turf
a chip is a small broken piece
Oz is the informal name for Australia

explanation.surface: A shellfish from Australia is flipped over in a bit of grass.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest here: the reversed piece sits in the fragment, and that whole unit sits in the turf.
explanation.definitionFit: Schizopods are small shrimp-like crustaceans such as opossum shrimps, named for their split limbs.

clue.text: Lignite extract needs day to go brown and develop

blocks.note: Mon is the short form of Monday, a day
to tan is to turn brown in the sun
to wax is to grow, as the moon does

explanation.surface: Instructions for a coal product: leave it a day to brown and mature.
explanation.definitionFit: Montan wax is a hard wax obtained by solvent extraction from lignite, the soft brown coal.

clue.text: Highlander offering loans with more liquidity to cover bills?

indicators.note: covering something means going around it, so the comparative wraps the bills

blocks.note: wetter means having more liquid
bills are posters or advertisements, ads

explanation.surface: A Scottish moneylender with plenty of ready cash is there to pay the bills.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface uses liquidity and bills in their money sense; in the wordplay liquidity is wetness and bills are posters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots law a wadsetter is the holder of a wadset, a mortgage on land, so a Scot who lends against property.

clue.text: Tart of fifty being hugged by lover

indicators.note: a thing hugged is held inside someone's arms, so the numeral goes inside the lover

blocks.note: a fan is a devotee or lover of something
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An unkind remark about a woman of fifty embraced by her admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: A flan is an open pastry case with a sweet or savoury filling, a kind of tart.

clue.text: Wish CERN could move to German city

indicators.note: letters that move change places, so the two words are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A hope that the CERN physics laboratory might relocate to a city in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Schwerin is the capital of the northern German state of Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, known for its lakeside castle.

clue.text: Baby orca, at intervals, repelled old gull

indicators.note: at intervals means every other one, so only alternate letters are taken
something repelled is driven back, so the chosen letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A young killer whale fights off an elderly seagull now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: BaBy OrCa gives BBOC, which reads backwards as COBB.
explanation.definitionFit: Cobb is an old dialect name for a gull, especially the great black-backed gull.

clue.text: Oil producer, not exactly happy in project

indicators.note: in puts the word for happy inside the word for project

blocks.note: ca is circa, approximately
to jut is to project or stick out
up means cheerful, in good spirits

explanation.surface: A firm making oil is lukewarm about its latest scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: CA + J(UP)UT. 'Project' looks like a noun in the surface but is the verb jut.
explanation.definitionFit: The cajuput is an Australasian paperbark tree whose leaves yield a pungent medicinal oil.

clue.text: Could corrupt suggestive, servile government?

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered, so the letters of the first word are mixed up

blocks.note: the letters taken as written
racy means risqué or mildly suggestive

explanation.surface: Could a fawning administration be both corrupt and suggestive?
explanation.definitionFit: Dulocracy is rule by slaves or servants, from Greek doulos, a slave; the question mark flags the wordplay on servile.

clue.text: Attention seeker, revolting about regulation ultimately as teenager?

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of regulation is used
about means around, so the word for revolting goes round that letter

blocks.note: yo is a call to get someone's attention
ugly can mean repulsive or revolting
its final letter

explanation.surface: A teenager craving attention rebels against the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: YO + U(N)GLY. Revolting reads as rebelling in the surface but means repulsive here.
explanation.definitionFit: Youngly is an adverb meaning in a youthful way or early in life, so behaving like a teenager.

clue.text: Old country cousin of Meg, Beth, Amy & co?

blocks.note: these are the March sisters of Little Women, who along with their sister Jo make up Jo's family

explanation.surface: A question about a rustic relative of the March girls from Little Women.
explanation.walkthrough: Meg, Beth and Amy are the sisters of Jo March in Little Women, so they are JO'S KIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Joskin is an old slang word for a yokel or clumsy rustic, the sort of person called a country cousin.

clue.text: Technically speaking one shock finished off US casualty

blocks.note: a jar is a jolt or shock
gone means dead or finished
ER is the emergency room, the American name for a casualty department

explanation.surface: Technically speaking, one jolt killed off an American casualty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Technically speaking' looks like a sentence opener; with 'one' it is the definition. Casualty is the British name for a hospital's emergency department.
explanation.definitionFit: A jargoneer is someone who habitually uses jargon, the specialised technical language of a trade.

clue.text: Loaded truck’s heading just north of the border

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, so only the start of truck is taken

blocks.note: loaded is slang for very wealthy
the first letter

explanation.surface: A laden lorry is heading just over the Scottish border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the border' means in Scotland: the answer is the Scots spelling of right, in the sense of just or fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Richt is the Scots form of right, which can mean just, fair or correct.

clue.text: Two sad men off out — their hearts grieving for Scotland

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter, so each word gives up its centre

blocks.note: the middle letter of each of the five three-letter words

explanation.surface: Two unhappy men set off, their hearts heavy with sorrow for their homeland.
explanation.walkthrough: tWo sAd mEn oFf oUt yields WAEFU; 'for Scotland' marks the Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Waefu is the Scots form of woeful, meaning sorrowful or mournful, so grieving in Scots speech.

clue.text: Hump around pile of grass to make a buck

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the hump wraps the pile of grass

blocks.note: a hump is a fit of sulks, and so is a pet
a rick is a stack of hay

explanation.surface: Hauling a haystack about to earn a quick dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: P(RICK)ET. Both hump and pet mean a sulk, as in 'have the hump' or 'in a pet'. Buck in the surface is a dollar.
explanation.definitionFit: A pricket is a male fallow deer in its second year, with unbranched horns, so a young buck.

clue.text: My new Daimler’s first journey back? Stick with banger!

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the car maker's name is used
back means the word for a journey is written in the other direction

blocks.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
N is the abbreviation for new
the first letter
a go can be a trip or turn

explanation.surface: Showing off a new Daimler's first trip home, only to find it an old banger.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang both for a sausage and for a clapped-out old car; here it is the sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A corn dog is an American snack: a sausage on a stick coated in cornmeal batter and deep-fried.

clue.text: Welshman losing pounds from Irishman’s diet

indicators.note: losing means doing without, so the abbreviation for pounds is removed

blocks.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament, a diet being a legislative assembly
L, from libra, is the abbreviation for pounds

explanation.surface: A Welshman shedding a few pounds from an Irishman's eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Diet in the surface is food; in the wordplay it is a parliament, the Irish Dáil.
explanation.definitionFit: Dai is a common Welsh nickname for David, so crosswords use it to stand for any Welshman.

clue.text: Grand: and so entertaining that king’s companion

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them in, so the phrase for and so takes in the letter for grand

blocks.note: then can mean therefore, and so
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A splendid line about a royal favourite who is great fun to have around.
explanation.walkthrough: A grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars, conventionally shortened to G.
explanation.definitionFit: A thegn was an Anglo-Saxon nobleman who held land in return for service, often as an attendant of the king.

clue.text: Being plump, turn to DIY for exercising

indicators.note: exercising works things hard and moves them about, so these letters are put through new positions

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone overweight takes up home improvement as a form of exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotundity is roundness of figure, the noun for the state of being stout or chubby.
